method_notes: Where a tagged name matches the sibling authorities built in the same wave, the entry also carries place_ids[] (records/authorities/gazetteer.json) and person_ids[] (records/authorities/people.json). Surname-only matches resolve through those authorities' variant lists and should be read as inferred.

Sources: the dated_statements[] of the fifteen Soap Creek Valley monographs (zc-sc-m01..m15), the Historic Soap Creek Valley Auto Tour (zc-sc-autotour-1989), and the thesis record's chronology[] (Chapter V and Table 22) and dated_statements[] (zc-sc-thesis-1999).
Every entry's `statement` is the verbatim quotation as extracted by the reader agents, with its printed page. Nothing is paraphrased, shortened or corrected here.

Dates were normalized to {year, month?, day?, year_end?} with a `precision` of day | month | year | range | decade | approximate | era | unknown. `date` is an ISO-ish rendering (1962-10-12, 1942-02, 1930s, 1935/1936, 1853). Two-digit forms ('43, '30s) were expanded to 19xx from interview context and the expansion is recorded in date_normalization_method; 'World War I' and 'World War II' were given conventional spans (1914-1918, 1939-1945) and likewise recorded.

Deduplication is exact only: identical statement text on the same page of the same record. Statements by different narrators about the same event are kept as separate entries - that is the point of the chronology - and linked by a shared event_key.

event_key_type 'event' = one of the curated event keys (a named event or era in the valley's history, matched on the statement text and, for a small curated set of topics, on Bob's own chapter/section heading). event_key_type 'place-decade' = a weaker link assigned to an otherwise unmatched statement that names one valley place and falls in a known decade (e.g. 1930s-berry-creek). Entries matching neither carry event_key: null - a blank rather than a guess.

narrator is the speaker of the matched transcript turn (speaker_name as printed). Where the reader recorded only Q/A, the narrator or the session's interviewer is supplied and narrator_confidence is 'inferred'. Front-matter, captions and editorial notes in the monographs are attributed to 'Zybach (editorial)'; thesis entries to 'Zybach (thesis)'; Auto Tour entries to 'Zybach (Auto Tour)'.

places[] and people[] are the source record's own tags where the reader supplied them, unioned with literal (word-boundary) matches of that record's places_mentioned[] names and a collection-wide person-name vocabulary against the statement text. No coordinates, no identity resolution, no invented names.
conflict = true where two or more sources give different years (or different exact dates) for the same point event. Both readings are kept; neither is corrected. See `conflicts`.

Known limits: 49 statements (front matter, cover captions, photo captions) could not be matched to a transcript turn and are attributed editorially; the printed back indexes of m06 and m07 drift against the scanned pagination (page anchors here come from the transcript, not the index); printed p.107 is missing from m10 and pp.76-77 from m12 (scan gaps), so any dated statement on those pages is absent from the source records.
